exclusion_detail: All 18 compounds are made from the amino bis-coumarin 'b' (3,3'-((4-aminophenyl)methylene)bis(4-hydroxy-2H-chromen-2-one)), and both precursors 'a' (nitro) and 'b' are given in the Experimental as 'As we have reported in our previous article [40]' with no procedure; the reduction conditions appear nowhere in this paper.

lead.why: Abstract/SAR: compound 16 (4-CF3-phenyl thiadiazole, IC50 0.12 uM) is the most potent urease inhibitor; the docking section calls it 'the most active compound 16'.

notes: Without the previous-article preparation of 'b' the route cannot be written from this paper; every compound 1-18 shares that dependency, so none qualifies. The thiadiazole-forming step itself (CS2, THF, 3 h, then reflux with the aryl hydrazide) is described.
